# Who is the Premier League's best ever Ghanaian player?

![Image 29: Yeboah, Gyan and Essien, Ghanaian players](https://resources.premierleague.pulselive.com/photo-resources/2020/05/14/57bc766d-ec6b-4c5a-bc5a-51c59839dd82/BestPlayerNation_Ghana_lead.png?width=1440)

 14 May 2020 

Feature

Yeboah? Gyan? Essien? Choose your favourite star from the West African country to feature in the competition

Some exceptionally gifted players have come from overseas to light up the Premier League, and we are celebrating the talent that has arrived from a few selected nations.

###### Ghana

We are looking at the achievements of the Premier League's top Ghanaians and we want to know who you think has been the best.

A total of 25 players from the West African country have featured in the Premier League, with [Nii Lamptey](https://www.premierleague.com/players/846/Nii-Lamptey/overview) being the first when he represented [Aston Villa](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/2/Aston-Villa/overview) in September 1994.

[Tony Yeboah](https://www.premierleague.com/players/889/Anthony-Yeboah/overview)became the first Ghanaian goalscorer in the competition when he struck for [Leeds United](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/9/Leeds-United/overview) in February 1995.

It was one of 24 Premier League goals he scored, some of which were truly breathtaking.

Indeed, Yeboah's goal tally is the joint-highest among his countrymen but is close to being surpassed by[Jordan Ayew](https://www.premierleague.com/players/5595/Jordan-Ayew/overview).

The [Crystal Palace](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/6/Crystal-Palace/overview)forward has scored a career-high eight goals in the current campaign, boosting his total to 24 since his first came for [Aston Villa](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/2/Aston-Villa/overview) against a [Swansea City](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/45/Swansea-City/overview) side which featured his brother, [Andre Ayew](https://www.premierleague.com/players/5594/Andr%C3%A9-Ayew/overview).

In terms of appearances, [Michael Essien](https://www.premierleague.com/players/2890/player/overview)leads the way with 168 for[Chelsea](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/4/Chelsea/overview). The two-time champion is one of only three Ghanaians to lift the Premier League Trophy.

The others,[Jeffrey Schlupp](https://www.premierleague.com/players/8980/player/overview) and [Daniel Amartey](https://www.premierleague.com/players/12306/Daniel-Amartey/overview), were both part of [Leicester City](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/26/Leicester-City/overview)'s fairytale 2015/16 campaign.

###### Leading PL numbers for Ghanaians

| Appearances | Goals | Assists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Michael Essien | 168 | Tony Yeboah | 24 | Michael Essien | 10 |
| Jeffrey Schlupp | 143 | Jordan Ayew | 24 | Andre Ayew | 9 |
| Jordan Ayew | 128 | Andre Ayew | 21 | Jordan Ayew | 8 |
| John Pantsil | 94 | Michael Essien | 17 | Jeffrey Schlupp | 7 |
| Andre Ayew | 89 | Asamoah Gyan | 10 | Christian Atsu | 6 |
| Christian Atsu | 79 | Jeffrey Schlupp | 10 | Sulley Muntari | 5 |

Ghana's most-capped player and highest-ever goalscorer also made his mark on the Premier League.

While [Asamoah Gyan](https://www.premierleague.com/players/4188/Asamoah-Gyan/overview)'s time in the competition was brief, he reached 10 goals in one season for [Sunderland](https://www.premierleague.com/players/4188/player/overview), where he was joined on loan by his compatriot [Sulley Muntari](https://www.premierleague.com/players/3472/player/overview).

Three seasons prior Muntari had helped[Portsmouth](https://www.premierleague.com/clubs/37/Portsmouth/overview)to their highest-ever Premier League finish as ended the 2007/08 campaign in eighth place and won the FA Cup.

You can watch a video of great Ghanaian goals above, and have a look at some eye-catching numbers in the table, before voting on who you think is the Premier League's best ever player from Ghana.

# From Lucas Radebe to Lyle Foster: Every South African Premier League player

Every South African who has played in the Premier League, from Lucas Radebe and Benni McCarthy to Steven Pienaar and Lyle Foster.

![Image 3: Benni McCarthy celebrates a goal for Blackburn in the Premier League.](https://cdn.vivasport.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1280,quality=82,format=auto/images/rgEUEIqGJu47LcwUyVfWOQ/media-13b9a120-ef28-49e9-a04b-9559a669e18b-f72a35429b71d7f2/public)
Photo: IMAGO / Bildbyran

[By VIVASPORT™](https://vivasport.com/about) Published 20 Sept 2026 · 09:38 UTC

[Preferred source](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=vivasport.com)Share Save

Sixteen South Africans have played in the Premier League since it began in 1992. One of them was on the pitch for ten minutes.

That is fewer than it feels. English football has been part of the South African television diet for three decades, but only 16 players have actually crossed into the Premier League and made an appearance.

The list starts with two Mamelodi Sundowns teammates at Leeds and eventually narrows to players whose entire Premier League careers can be measured in minutes.

It also contains one of the country's greatest defenders, its leading Premier League goalscorer and the player who holds the appearance record by some distance.

## Leeds got their bet backwards

Lucas Radebe and Phil Masinga arrived at Leeds United from Mamelodi Sundowns in 1994, and the story goes that the club initially regarded Masinga as the more promising signing.

Masinga became the first South African to play in the Premier League when he came on against West Ham. He scored against Chelsea a week later, the first goal by a South African in the competition. He eventually left after 31 league appearances and five goals.

Radebe stayed for a decade.

[![Image 4: Lucas Radebe: South Africa's captain fantastic](https://cdn.vivasport.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=960,quality=82,format=auto/images/rgEUEIqGJu47LcwUyVfWOQ/media-2f2498ad-6f87-41ce-aa63-acd0b0d7845e-2e678b56efc28f12/public)Player Profile Lucas Radebe: South Africa's captain fantastic 2026-06-18T06:42:22.000Z](https://vivasport.com/football/stories/lucas-radebe-bafana-chief-leeds-united-legend)

He made 197 Premier League appearances, captained Leeds in the Champions League and became one of the most respected figures in the club's history. There is still a suite at Elland Road named after him.

He never scored a Premier League goal.

Nobody has ever thought that mattered.

The two men established a route that others would follow, but the next generation produced a very different kind of South African presence.

## The Charlton years

Mark Fish arrived in England at Bolton Wanderers in 1997 after leaving Lazio. His first Premier League season ended in relegation, but he returned to the division with Charlton in 2000 and went on to make 124 appearances and score four goals.

Shaun Bartlett joined him at Charlton, initially on loan before making the move permanent. He spent six seasons there and finished with 123 Premier League appearances and 24 goals.

His volley against Leicester in 2000-01 remains one of the enduring highlights of the South African Premier League generation.

Eric Tinkler had a much shorter stay. He played 25 Premier League matches for Barnsley during their only season in the competition and scored twice.

One of those goals came against Fish's Bolton.

The South African contingent was beginning to become more than a curiosity.

## McCarthy set the scoring standard

Benni McCarthy remains the South African Premier League goalscorer nobody has come close to catching.

He scored 37 goals in 120 appearances for Blackburn Rovers and West Ham United, including 18 league goals in his first Blackburn season in 2006-07. He finished second in the Golden Boot race behind Didier Drogba.

That remains the best scoring season by a South African in the Premier League.

[![Image 5: Inside Benni McCarthy's Career](https://cdn.vivasport.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=960,quality=82,format=auto/images/rgEUEIqGJu47LcwUyVfWOQ/media-a2fb08ce-a6e2-44a6-bf4f-c3de564b83f4-19db2e3b664c59d2/public)Player Profile Inside Benni McCarthy's Career 2026-06-17T19:43:45.000Z](https://vivasport.com/football/stories/benni-mccarthy-career-records-legacy)

Aaron Mokoena was in the same Blackburn squad and provided the less glamorous half of the equation. He eventually made 124 Premier League appearances for Blackburn and Portsmouth without scoring.

The two are level on appearances with Fish, but their statistical profiles could hardly be more different.

Quinton Fortune occupies another unique place in the history. He remains the only South African to play for Manchester United, making 82 Premier League appearances for United and Bolton and scoring five goals.

## Pienaar was the high-water mark

Steven Pienaar is the South African Premier League record holder.

He made 214 appearances across Everton, Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland and scored 20 goals. He is the only South African to pass 200 appearances and the only one to play for three Premier League clubs.

Everton was where he made his name.

His two spells at Goodison Park accounted for the overwhelming majority of his Premier League career and established him as one of the country's most successful exports to English football.

After Pienaar, the list gets progressively thinner.

Kagisho Dikgacoi made 39 appearances for Fulham and Crystal Palace. He was sent off on his Premier League debut and never scored.

Mbulelo Mabizela made seven appearances for Tottenham and scored on his debut against Leicester before playing only six more times.

Tokelo Rantie made three appearances for Bournemouth.

Percy Tau made three for Brighton after a lengthy wait for the work permit that allowed him to finally play in England.

And then there was Khanya Leshabela.

He came off the bench for Leicester City in a 5-0 win over Sheffield United in March 2021 and played for roughly ten minutes.

That is the entire Premier League career of the 16th South African.

## The 16, ranked by appearances

| Rank | Player | Premier League clubs | Appearances | Goals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Steven Pienaar | Everton, Tottenham Hotspur, Sunderland | 214 | 20 |

| 6 | Benni McCarthy | Blackburn Rovers, West Ham United | 120 | 37 |
| 7 | Quinton Fortune | Manchester United, Bolton Wanderers | 82 | 5 |
| 8 | Lyle Foster | Burnley | 50 | 8 |
| 9 | Kagisho Dikgacoi | Fulham, Crystal Palace | 39 | 0 |

| 14 | Percy Tau | Brighton & Hove Albion | 3 | 0 |
| 15 | Tokelo Rantie | Bournemouth | 3 | 0 |
| 16 | Khanya Leshabela | Leicester City | 1 | 0 |

Nine of the 16 scored at least once, and together they have 106 Premier League goals.

McCarthy accounts for 37 of them.

Lyle Foster is the latest name on the list. His four-season Burnley spell ended in September 2026 when he joined Houston Dynamo on loan through June 2027.

## The ones who were on the books, but never played

There is another category.

Pierre Issa was on Chelsea's books without making a competitive appearance. Matthew Booth was at Wimbledon but never played in the Premier League.

Bongani Khumalo spent four and a half years contracted to Tottenham without making a competitive appearance for the club.

They are close enough to the Premier League to make the distinction interesting, but not close enough to enter the 16.

Then there are the South Africans who complicate the definition altogether.

## The ones who got away

Roy Wegerle was born in Pretoria but represented the United States after becoming a naturalised American. He played 64 Premier League matches for Blackburn Rovers and Coventry City and scored 13 goals.

Had birthplace rather than football nationality been the only criterion, he would sit comfortably inside the main list.

Bruce Grobbelaar was born in Durban and became a Zimbabwe international. He played for Liverpool through the early Premier League years before later appearing for Southampton, having already won six league titles and the European Cup.

Mark Stein, born in Cape Town, scored 21 goals in 42 Premier League appearances for Chelsea across his first two seasons.

Mark Gonzalez was born in Durban but represented Chile after leaving South Africa as a child.

Andrew Surman was born in Johannesburg and went on to play 144 Premier League matches for four clubs, but turned down approaches to represent South Africa.

And then there is Sean Dundee.

Born in Durban, Dundee left for Germany at 19 and eventually earned a move to Liverpool after scoring freely for Karlsruher.

He made three Premier League appearances without scoring.

Dundee had already turned down South Africa, believing Germany might eventually come calling.

They never did.

For all the years South Africans have spent watching the Premier League, the country's actual footprint in it remains remarkably small.

Sixteen players.
